UA1_Tpdf-G2_F03.reason: Whether a graphic stands in for text is a question about the picture, not about the file: nothing distinguishes a figure that spells a word from one that shows a shape. The check reports the figure and what its tagged content actually paints.

uncovered.title: Real content correctly tagged
Decorative content correctly marked as artifact

UA1_Tpdf-G3_F01.reason: Whether content is real or decorative is the author's answer and no entry records it. The check reports the artifact text that continues a tagged sentence, with the neighbour it runs on from.

UA1_Tpdf-G3_F02.reason: Same judgement, the whole-paragraph case: the check reports a declared artifact carrying a sentence's worth of words at the document's own body size.

UA1_Tpdf-G3_F03.reason: Whether a background is decoration is not decidable from the tree. The check reports the figure and the fact that its tagged content paints no text.

UA1_Tpdf-G4_F01.reason: Tag order IS the reading order; geometry only disagrees with it. The check reports the disagreement and its size, and never decides which of the two the author meant.

UA1_Tpdf-G4_F02.reason: The same disagreement, between marked content sequences inside one tag. Reported with its inventory rather than judged.

UA1_Tpdf-G4_F03.reason: A column boundary is a layout fact, not an order. The check reports the marked content sequence whose runs reach across one, which is what a page-wide top-to-bottom sort cannot see.

UA1_Tpdf-G4_F04.reason: Where a sidebar belongs in the reading order is an editorial decision. Reported as a disagreement with geometry.

UA1_Tpdf-G4_F05.reason: Order INSIDE one marked content sequence: the check reports runs that share a line and draw right to left, which is evidence and not a verdict, because a rotated or bidirectional layout draws that way legitimately.

uncovered.title: H1 heading appropriately tagged
Similar real content appropriately tagged
Visually-separated content appropriately tagged
Multiline content appropriately tagged

UA1_Tpdf-G5_F01.reason: Whether a paragraph is a heading is a semantic; the drawn size is the only signal a file carries, and a size is not a semantic. The check reports the paragraph with its size and the body size.

UA1_Tpdf-G5_F02.reason: Whether two blocks of text are one paragraph is the author's answer. The check reports the element whose own content is separated by more than the line pitch it sets.

UA1_Tpdf-G5_F03.reason: Whether a figure interrupts one semantic unit is a judgement about the prose. The check reports the figure sitting between two elements of the same role.

UA1_Tpdf-G5_F04.reason: Visual separation is not semantic separation. The check reports the element whose blocks are set apart and leaves the reading to a person.

UA1_Tpdf-G5_F05.reason: Whether adjacent lines are one unit is the author's answer. The check reports same-role siblings occupying adjacent lines of one block.

UA1_Tpdf-H_F01.reason: A first-level heading tagged as a paragraph is only detectable through how it is set. The check reports the paragraph, its size and the body size.

UA1_Tpdf-H_F02.reason: Whether two headings are one heading over two lines is a judgement about the text. Reported with the measurements.

UA1_Tpdf-H_F03.reason: A paragraph tagged as a heading reads as a heading to every reader; only the drawn size disagrees. The check reports the heading set no larger than the body.

UA1_Tpdf-H_F05.reason: A heading tagged as a paragraph one level below H_F01's case: still a semantic no entry in the file records. The check reports the paragraph with its drawn size and the document's body size.

UA1_Tpdf-H_F07.reason: Whether a document's title and its first section heading are the same level is editorial. The check reports that more than one top-level heading exists.

UA1_Tpdf-L_F02.reason: A label left inside its own body is still text in the right place; only the author knows it was meant to be a label. The check reports the item whose body opens with a list marker and carries no Lbl.

UA1_Tpdf-L_F06.reason: Whether a run of paragraphs IS a list is a judgement about the content. The check reports consecutive paragraphs opening with list markers under no list element.

UA1_Tpdf-L_F08.reason: Whether substructure belongs inside one body or beside it is the author's answer. The check reports adjacent sibling lists declaring the same numbering.

UA1_Tpdf-L_F10.reason: A list continuing across a page break and two lists that happen to adjoin are the same shape in the tree. Reported, not decided.
